content.text: Classical logic has two truth values. **Many-valued logics** add more.
Jan Łukasiewicz gave a third value, indeterminate, to statements about the future, like 'there will be a sea battle tomorrow'. Fuzzy logic allows every degree from 0 to 1.

examples.title: Three-valued negation
examples.note: Denying something indeterminate leaves it indeterminate.

examples.title: Fuzzy truth
lines: A person 1.80 m tall might be tall to degree 0.7.
examples.note: Vague words like tall come in degrees.

question.prompt: Why did Łukasiewicz add a third truth value?
question.hint: Think of the sea battle tomorrow.
question.explanation: He wanted a value for statements about the future, which seem neither true nor false yet.
